repairs.text: Strongest feature: Hernandez’s beach simulation isolates a precise inference: artificially stimulating an experience resembling seaside perception cannot deductively establish that every uninduced experience in the category lacks a corresponding external object. Principal limitation: This rebuttal defeats only Aron Ra’s universal inference from neurological reproducibility; it offers no affirmative evidence that any spontaneous out-of-body report involves genuine separation, where comparative explanatory probability is decisive. Live burden: Hernandez must identify documented cases whose perceptual accuracy, inaccessible information, and controlled circumstances remain less expected under neural, psychological, or ordinary informational explanations, then show why separation predicts those details. Locked score: The locked score of 82 remains warranted because the analogy is clear, disciplined, and directly responsive, while establishing only a boundary on an overextended objection rather than support for the soul.

Strongest feature: Aron Ra answers the beach analogy at the evidential level: predictable false out-of-body impressions caused by physical brain intervention positively support neural generation, beyond merely showing that simulation is logically possible. Principal limitation: Producing some deceptive impressions does not show every similar spontaneous report is entirely physical, and he supplies neither experimental controls nor criteria for establishing adequate similarity between induced and reported cases. Live burden: He must quantify how predictable brain induction changes the relative likelihood of neural production against genuine separation, restrict the conclusion to relevantly matched experiences, and address differences between laboratory suggestion and uncontrolled testimony. Locked score: The locked score of 80 fits because the reply is coherent, direct, and probative, but categorical metaphysical language and absent methodology exceed its evidence.
